items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe reflected on her experience at Crow Shield Lodge last month.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.

items.title: Today we recognize the International Day of Persons with Disabilities,
notes: which takes place each year on December 3. We also recognize that Indigenous Disability Awareness Month comes to a close at the end of November. These observances promote the rights and wellbeing of persons with disabilities, as well as to celebrate the contributions of disabled people to political, social, economic and cultural life.
Disability is a broad term: there are many different types of disabilities, they can be visible or invisible, present from birth or acquired later in life.

Each person’s experience of disability is unique, and impacted by other aspects of identity. It is all too universal though the ongoing experience of barriers that keep people with disabilities from participating fully at work, school, play and in civic life.

As policy makers and service providers, we must acknowledge, address and remove these barriers. Including accessible features in our buildings, creating websites that work well with screen readers, and using plain language to describe our services are just a few of the things we can do to make our city more accessible.

We all have a role to play in creating a city that brings an end to ableism and increases inclusivity. We encourage you to take in the resources and upcoming events offered by the Waterloo Public Library, follow disabled leaders and creators on social media and join the calls for change when needed. The imperative of incorporating accessible design and approaches into our day-to-day lives is clear when we consider that we are all temporarily able-bodied.
As a City, we re-commit ourselves to the long-term work of confronting ableism and removing barriers in order to create a community where everyone can participate, contribute, belong and thrive.

items.title: It is with great sadness I learned about the passing of former city
notes: Councillor Morty Taylor. A dedicated community leader, he served as City Councillor for Ward 4 in Waterloo from 1991 to 1997 and 2000 to 2003. As a resident of Waterloo for over 60 years, Morty was also very well known in our city as the friendly, respected business person who founded Morty's Pub at the corner of King and University in 1981.

His commitment to our city and the Ward 4 student community extended to serving on the boards of various local organizations, including Wilfrid Laurier University, Waterloo Library, Oktoberfest Advisory Council, Project Lift, the Kitchener Waterloo Symphony, Recreation and Leisure 55 Plus, The Waterloo Student Housing Task Force and The Affordable Housing Task Force.

As a businessman and a member of council, Morty made a significant contribution to the City of Waterloo and will be missed. On behalf of my council colleagues and residents of the city, I extend my condolences to Morty’s family and friends.
Flags at City of Waterloo facilities will be at half-mast in memory of former Councillor Taylor until sunset on November 27, 2023.

items.title: Regional All-Council Closed Meeting (Education and Training) –
notes: December 8, 2023, 1:00pm

Councillor Hanmer mentioned that the Westvale association held a Family Skate at Albert McCormick Community Centre this past weekend (November 25/26). It was very well attended and she thanked the staff and the Westvale executive for organizing.

Councillor Roe wanted to mention that the May Court Club kicked off their Christmas Dreams Raffle at Conestoga mall on November 21st, supporting KidsAbility, the Grand River Hospital Foundation’s Postpartum Wellness Program, and Make-A-Wish Canada.
Councillor Roe also brought up that on Saturday, November 25th, the KW Titans partnered with the local YMCAs and Food Bank to collect donations and give away tickets to their games.

Councillor Wright shared that the Waterloo Public Library approved their strategic plan this past week, the first strategic plan they’ve had in many years. It’ll be made public soon, but it’s well-aligned with the City’s strategic plan.

Mayor McCabe mentioned that the Waterloo main library is holding an Archive of Experience: Living Library on November 30th at 1:30p.m. There is also a second panel, Disabled vs. Disabling, being held on December 1st at 12:00p.m.
Councillor Wright also mentioned that the Aging Well Waterloo publication was just released and is available at the library and digitally.

Councillor Roe wanted to mention the lighting of the Christmas Tree in Waterloo Town Square is this Friday December 1st, and there is also an art market happening on December 1st and 2nd. The lights in Waterloo Park are also up for the Wonders of Winter.

Mayor McCabe mentioned she was at an economic development retreat in Germany with the Mayors of Cambridge and Kitchener, as well as a member of the Economic Development staff. It was a fantastic opportunity to meet companies who’ve made investments in Waterloo, discuss challenges, and answer questions.
